title: Smoke & Carbon Monoxide
summary: Get people out to fresh air if you can do it safely, call for help, and suspect carbon monoxide when several people in the same place feel unwell.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} for smoke or carbon monoxide exposure
when: Anyone who has breathed smoke or fumes and is unwell
Headache, dizziness, nausea, confusion or drowsiness in several people in the same place or vehicle
Burns around the mouth or nose, soot, hoarse voice

steps.title: Do not become a casualty
steps.text: Do not enter smoke, a burning building or a space with fumes. Carbon monoxide has no smell.

steps.title: Get to fresh air
steps.text: If safe, move people out and open doors and windows. Turn off engines, generators or heaters if safe.

steps.title: Call {EMERGENCY}
steps.text: Tell them carbon monoxide or smoke is suspected.

steps.title: Check breathing
steps.text: If not breathing normally, start CPR. If breathing but unresponsive, recovery position.

steps.title: Oxygen
steps.text: Give oxygen if available and you are trained.

steps.title: Monitor
steps.text: Watch for hoarse voice, coughing or breathing difficulty – airway swelling can develop later.

doNot: Do not enter a smoke- or fume-filled area
Do not run engines or generators in enclosed spaces
Do not let them return inside until it has been cleared
